sections.h2: Which Athens office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
The Athens-Clarke County Tax Commissioner mails and collects the bill, and the county's Board of Assessors decides the value. Athens is a consolidated city and county, so one unified government covers the whole of Clarke County except Winterville and part of Bogart, and the same two offices serve every Athens address.

The Tax Commissioner works from Room 250 of the courthouse at 325 East Washington Street, takes mail at PO Box 1768 in Athens, and answers at 706-613-3120. The Assessors' office handles questions about value, appeals and site visits at 706-613-3140. The tag office on Lexington Road cannot take property tax payments at its counter, though it has a drop box for checks and money orders.

  • Bill lookups and online payments run through athensclarketax.com.
  • A second drop box sits at the courthouse lower-level entrance.
  • A bill that never arrives is no excuse for paying late, because the county mails to the last known address.

sections.h2: Due dates, penalties and where the money goes
sections.html:
Bills go out in late summer and the usual due date for real estate and business personal property is October 20. A balance left open after that accrues interest and penalties. Late balances carry a 5 percent penalty every 120 days past the due date, up to four times, for a total of 20 percent, and Georgia law requires late fees on any bill not paid by the deadline.

Money from the bill goes to the Clarke County Board of Education, the unified government and the State of Georgia. The general fund rate is 12.25 mills, and a separate 1 mill levy applies to real property in the downtown area under the Downtown Development Authority.

Athens is a college town where tenants outnumber owners, and that shapes who shops for a house. Owners hold 40.7 percent of the 53,643 households. The middle owner-occupied home is worth $299,200, and the middle gross rent is $1,219 a month. The 2025 estimate is 128,612 residents. A seller here may meet investors and landlords as often as families, and rental-ready condition can matter to them.

A real estate return on form PT-50R goes to the Tax Commissioner in courthouse Room 250 during the first three months of any year in which the property changed hands or was improved, with April 1 as the last day. Owners with no changes may skip the return. Missing a required return brings a 10 percent penalty on the unreturned value, plus interest.

Business equipment and other personal property must be returned to the Board of Assessors every year by April 1. Challenges to a value or a denied exemption start with the Board of Assessors, and an appeal that ends without agreement moves automatically to the Board of Equalization. Assessor staff also inspect properties with active building permits, recent sales and open appeals.

The state allows 45 days from the day the assessment notice is mailed. In Athens that same window also closes the door on homestead applications, so one date does double duty.

The standard Athens exemption removes $2,000 at the state level, $25,000 from the county maintenance and operations levy and $10,000 from the school levy. The county portion rose to $25,000 as of 2023.

The home must be your owner-occupied main residence at the start of the year. Apply in person at the Tax Commissioner's office. The deadline is the same 45-day window used for appeals, which typically opens with notices mailed in mid-May. Miss it, and the exemption waits for the next tax year.

  • Changing the deed, for example by moving the home into a trust or adding a spouse, means applying again.
  • A low-income exemption and several age-based and veteran exemptions exist for qualifying owners.
  • A one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant appears only on the 2026 bill, not on the assessment notice.

sections.h2: What happens to the bill if you sell this year?
sections.html:
Even after a sale, the bill goes to whoever owned the home when the year began. New owners should call the Tax Commissioner for payment instructions, and sellers who receive a bill after selling should call too, so the account does not turn up as delinquent.

Buyers should verify before closing that no taxes are owed, because attorneys check real estate balances but can overlook personal property such as boats or business equipment. A seller who owes back taxes should phone 706-613-3120 for a payoff total and hand it to the title company, which can settle the account out of the proceeds.

Georgia allows no refund for a partial year of ownership. Unpaid taxes that reach the collection stage can lead to levy and sale of the property. Selling before that point keeps the sale in your control and the balance on the closing statement.

A short checklist helps. Look up your parcel on athensclarketax.com to see the balance. Confirm your homestead is on file. Call the Assessors at 706-613-3140 if a recent permit or improvement may have changed the value. Then ask the Tax Commissioner for a payoff in writing and give it to the closing attorney.

A cash buyer can close quickly, but the payoff total and the personal property check still have to be done first, so start them before you accept an offer.

If you want to apply for a homestead exemption on a home you just bought, go to Room 250 in person and bring proof that the house is your main residence. Do not wait for the notice if you already know the deadline is close, because the same 45-day window that governs appeals also governs the application, and a missed window pushes the savings out a full year.

Owners who change the deed, for example by adding a spouse, should plan the new application before the next notices mail. Sellers who are moving a home into a trust before listing should check with the Tax Commissioner first, since the change can reset the exemption and leave the first bill after closing higher than expected.

faqs.q: How much is the Athens-Clarke County millage rate?
faqs.a: The general fund rate is 12.25 mills for Athens-Clarke County government. Downtown real property carries an extra 1 mill levy, and school and state levies are billed separately on the same statement.

faqs.q: Where can I mail an Athens property tax payment?
faqs.a: Mail it to the Tax Commissioner at PO Box 1768, Athens, GA 30603. You can also pay online at athensclarketax.com, in person in courthouse Room 250 or in a drop box, using checks or money orders only in the drop box.

faqs.q: Did the 2026 Athens bill include any one-time credit?
faqs.a: Yes. A one-time Homeowners Tax Relief Grant is applied to 2026 bills for each qualifying homestead. It shows up on the tax bill, not on the assessment notice.

faqs.q: Do I need a new homestead application if I add someone to the deed?
faqs.a: Yes. An approved exemption stays in place while you own and occupy the home, but a change in ownership, such as adding a spouse to the deed or moving the home into a trust, requires a new application.

faqs.q: Which number do I use to question my Athens value?
faqs.a: Phone the Assessors at 706-613-3140, then put the appeal in writing within 45 days of the notice date. Without an agreement, the county sends it on to the Board of Equalization.
